text:
alex: Quick question — I'm switching auth-proxy service from ClusterIP -> NodePort to support an NLB TLS passthrough canary. Noticed AWS target group health checks are hitting targetPort 8080 but our container is listening on 8443 (TLS). Any gotchas before I roll this?

mira: ah yep. TLS passthrough means NLB won't terminate, so health-check protocol matters. If you used HTTP health checks they might probe the wrong port/protocol.

alex: we set healthcheck protocol to TCP in the TF change but AWS console shows the target registered on port 8080 still. K8s Service YAML maps port: 443 -> targetPort: 8443, containerPort: 8443.

sam: is the service using targetPort by name or number? If targetPort is a named port, make sure pod containerPort has that exact name. Otherwise kube may map unexpectedly.

alex: targetPort is numeric 8443 in the manifest. Here's the service snippet I pushed in the PR:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: auth-proxy
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: "tcp"
spec:
  type: NodePort
  ports:
    - port: 443
      targetPort: 8443
      protocol: TCP
      nodePort: 32080
  selector:
    app: auth-proxy
  externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
```

mira: couple suggestions: 1) set externalTrafficPolicy: Local if you care about source IP and want node-targeted health checks to succeed without kube-proxy DNAT. 2) For health checks, either use TCP health check on the target group or configure a separate HTTP health port (unencrypted) that the NLB can probe.

sam: also check the AWS annotation `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-port`. It defaults to traffic-port but sometimes controller chooses NodePort. For NLB+NodePort the health check often probes the NodePort on the nodes.

alex: interesting — so AWS might be probing NodePort (32080) but console shows 8080 because the target group was created from previous config? Could be stale.

mira: yep stale target group mapping is common when you change service ports quickly. If the controller didn't recreate TG, you'll get old ports. Delete the service to force reconciliation or update annotations to force new TG.

opsbot: deploy-bot: note: cluster-controller detected service port change for auth-proxy, scheduled target group reconciliation in 5m.

alex: I also saw some docs referencing `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-protocol: tls` — but NLB TLS health checks don't do TLS handshake, they only do TCP/TLS on the socket? Confusing.

sam: NLB supports TCP/TLS health checks at the target group level, but if you set PROXY protocol or TLS you need to ensure backend speaks TLS. For passthrough it's fine to use TCP health checks (simpler).

mira: If you need layer7 checks (path, 200) you need ALB or terminate TLS at the LB and use HTTP/HTTPS healthchecks. With passthrough you lose HTTP-level checks.

alex: ok switching healthcheck --> TCP and setting externalTrafficPolicy: Local. One last thing — what about security group for NodePort? I assume NLB attaches to node SG and needs the NodePort allowed (32080).

sam: correct. Make sure nodes SG allows inbound from NLB on the NodePort. If you're on EKS, control plane often manages that but double-check.

alex: noted. I'll: 1) change healthcheck protocol to TCP in TF, 2) set externalTrafficPolicy: Local, 3) ensure node SG allows 32080, 4) trigger TG reconcile. Doing a canary on cluster-1.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started for auth-proxy on cluster-1 (namespace: infra-canary). Observing health for 10m. :eyes:

mira: ping if you need me to flip to HTTP health endpoint later — we can add a small /health on 8080 and have the NLB probe that if you want l7 checks after terminating TLS elsewhere.

alex: thanks — will report back. If anyone wants to eyeball the TF diff it's at https://git.internal/redwood/infra/+/refs/changes/2345

sam: one more tiny note: avoid using low NodePorts that collision with other services. 32080 is fine but put it in our NodePort range in the cluster config.

alex: good call. I'll update PR with these notes and add a short checklist in the PR description so reviewers know what to validate.

mira: :thumbsup:
